subject: mathematics
question_text: If A is the matrix with rows (2, −4) and (−5, 3), then find A + A′ and AA′.

verification.note: Source: Baby Bullet-Q, Junior Inter Maths-1A (Sri Publishers, Machilipatnam), book p.84 — VSAQ chapter 15 Matrices, answer 106. Printed appearances: AP 18,19. ⚠ THE 1+1 SPLIT IS OURS, NOT THE BOOK'S — no [N Marks] tags are printed against this answer. recall_prompt: Say how you would find both of these — say what A dash is first.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Write A′ and add
steps.margin_note: First mark. A′ is the transpose: rows become columns. Then A + A′ is an ordinary entry-by-entry addition.
steps.memory_tip: A′ swaps rows for columns; then A + A′ is an ordinary entry-by-entry addition.

recall.must_convey: That A′ is the transpose (rows become columns) and that A + A′ is found by adding entry by entry.
accept: A dash is the transpose so rows become columns then add entry by entry
write the transpose by swapping rows and columns and add it to A
transpose A first then add the two matrices
A dash ante transpose, rows columns swap, tarvata add cheyyali
the transpose swaps the off diagonal entries then you add

steps.why: Transposing reflects the matrix across its principal diagonal. The diagonal entries never move, which is why only the −4 and −5 swap here.
common_mistakes: Transposing by reversing the rows instead of swapping rows with columns.

steps.label: Multiply A by A′
steps.margin_note: Second mark, and a different operation from the first — this one is row against column, not entry by entry. Both answers come out symmetric, which is worth noticing.
steps.memory_tip: A different operation from the first: row against COLUMN, not entry by entry.

lines.text: ∴ A + A′ and AA′ are as above

recall.must_convey: That AA′ is a matrix MULTIPLICATION, row against column, giving rows (20, −22) and (−22, 34).
accept: A A dash is a multiplication row into column giving twenty minus twenty two and minus twenty two thirty four
multiply A by its transpose using row into column
this one is a product not a sum so multiply row by column
A into A dash multiply cheste twenty minus twenty two vasthundi
the product of A with its transpose is a symmetric matrix

steps.why: The question asks for one ADDITION and one MULTIPLICATION. Doing the same operation twice is the commonest way to lose this mark.
common_mistakes: Adding A and A′ again instead of multiplying.
